title: Capacity Command Center: granular throughput knobs, predictive autoscale, and audit stream
creator: Sofia Park
description: Goal: Ship a unified Console experience (Capacity Command Center) for Dedicated fleets that combines direct throughput controls (per-fleet and per-route), predictive autoscaling policies, and an immutable change history/audit stream. This ticket covers PM requirements, acceptance criteria, stakeholder sign-offs, and rollout plan for the UI + API surface needed to operate throughput guarantees and autoscale policies without deep infra knowledge.
background: Customers running Dedicated capacity have asked for a single-pane operations view: a way to set hard throughput guarantees (tokens/sec), create workload-aware autoscale policies, preview cost impact, and see a chronological audit of changes with rollbacks. Current console panels are fragmented (preset toggles, separate autoscale editor, and an opaque activity log). This initiative targets platform parity across Hosted/Dedicated while preserving reserved commit constraints.
scope:
- New Capacity Command Center page under Fleet > Capacity
- Per-fleet throughput controls with explicit SLA target, burst allowance, and estimated cost delta
- Autoscaling policy builder: schedule, reactive rules (p50/p90 latency, queue depth, token burn rate), and cooldown windows
- Predictive scaling preview using last 7/30 day workload patterns (UI-only initially)
- Immutable change history stream with diff view and rollback link to previous policy version
- API endpoints for programmatic changes and audit retrieval (backwards compatible)
out_of_scope:
- Implementing backend predictive autoscaler (only UI preview in this phase)
- Deep billing integration for committed discounts (cost deltas are estimates)
- Private on-prem packaged installer changes (handled in follow-up)
acceptance_criteria: Capacity Command Center accessible from Fleet nav and shows list of fleets with current throughput targets and health indicators
PM-set throughput target can be edited inline, saved as a new policy version, and pushed to runtime with confirmation modal
Autoscaling policy builder supports at least three rule types: scheduled (cron), reactive-latency (p90 > threshold), and reactive-throughput (queue depth) with cooldown and max/min bounds
Preview shows predicted scaling events for last 7-day workload and shows estimated token cost delta for a chosen policy
Change history stores every policy change with user, timestamp, diff, and an affordance to rollback to a previous version (audit only; rollback triggers existing API)
All actions are logged to the audit endpoint and visible in the Console -> Activity stream within 60s
E2E tests for editing throughput, creating autoscale policies, and viewing history are added to console e2e suite
Design and PM sign-off on copy, layout, and failure states (low-data, backend errors)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Operators accidentally set throughput above committed capacity and cause billing disputes. Mitigation: add guardrail that shows committed capacity and requires a two-step confirmation with explicit cost delta when exceeding commit.
Risk: Predictive preview misleads customers. Mitigation: label previews as estimates and include confidence band; do not auto-apply predictive changes in this phase.
Risk: Large fleets cause UI performance issues. Mitigation: paginate fleet list, lazy-load charts, and surface sampling for long histories.
Risk: Audit log growth and storage cost. Mitigation: retention policy defaults (90 days) with export to S3/enterprise archive option.

Risk: Ambiguity about precedence between policy types (scheduled vs reactive). Mitigation: define precedence rules in UI help text and tooltips; schedule wins unless overridden by emergency override feature (future ticket).
implementation_notes: Frontend: React + ChartJS for throughput timelines; reuse Fleet table component; new PolicyEditor modal component
Backend: Add policy-version resource and policy-applier proxy endpoint; events written to audit stream on write
API: POST /fleets/{id}/policies to create versioned policy, PATCH to update, GET /fleets/{id}/policies?version=latest
Telemetry: emit events capacity.policy.update, capacity.throughput.set, capacity.policy.rollback with metadata for cost estimate
qa_plan: Manual tests for save/rollback flows and confirmation modals
Automated e2e: create policy -> simulate metric breach -> ensure reactive rule would trigger (mock metrics)
Load test: UI list with 5k fleets to validate pagination and chart sampling
Security: verify audit export only accessible to org-admin role
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal dogfood on staging with two engineering customers and internal SREs (2 weeks)
Beta: opt-in in production for customers with Dedicated capacity (feature flag)
GA: enable for all Dedicated customers with opt-out for enterprise customers requiring custom retention
Monitoring: SLOs for API latency (95th < 200ms) and UI load times (95th < 600ms)
notes: Decision 2025-02-20: keep predictive autoscaler UI-only for now to reduce risk and speed delivery (agreed by SRE and Research)
Feedback 2025-02-28 from Sales: expose a read-only cost breakdown graph for sales demos (low-effort)
